title: The Milky Way above the ELT site
caption: The Milky Way above the Extremely Large Telescope construction site, Cerro Armazones, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Countless stars, along with the Milky Way's hazy band, shine clearly above the construction site of the Extremely Large Telescope on Cerro Armazones in Chile. Seeing the Milky Way this distinctly takes a place with little light pollution, like this mountain, and a night with little or no moonlight.

When it starts operating, the ELT will be 'the world's biggest eye on the sky'. With a 39-metre primary mirror, it will search in optical and near-infrared light for new exoplanets, especially Earth-like planets orbiting other stars. It will also carry out a kind of 'stellar archaeology', tackling basic questions about how planets, the first stars, early galaxies and black holes form and evolve.

Perhaps its most exciting goal is to measure directly how quickly the Universe's expansion is speeding up. Astronomers have known for decades that galaxies are moving apart, and now think the expansion is accelerating; measuring that directly would greatly deepen our understanding of the Universe.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken at the ELT construction site on Cerro Armazones, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears brighter than it would to someone at the site.
